walkthroughs.body_html:
World Religions: Judaism / Islam / Buddhism / Hinduism — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

World Religions: Judaism / Islam / Buddhism / Hinduism brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with World Religions: Judaism / Islam / Buddhism / Hinduism.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

Judaism
Islam
Hinduism
The first five books of the Hebrew Bible

A Hindu epic poem

Liberation from the cycle of rebirth

Puja
Keeping kosher

mcqs.q: Is the Buddha worshipped as a creator god in Buddhism?
options: Buddhists worship the Buddha as the god who created the world.
No — the Buddha was a human teacher who attained enlightenment; Buddhists revere him as a guide rather than worshipping him as a creator god.
The Buddha is the Hindu god of wisdom.
Muhammad is the Arabic name Muslims use for God.

mcqs.q: Is Hinduism simply the worship of many unrelated gods?
options: Hindus worship only one god called Krishna and reject all others.
Hinduism is pure polytheism with millions of separate, unconnected gods.
No — many Hindus understand the various deities as expressions of one supreme reality, Brahman, so Hinduism can be seen as one ultimate divine behind many forms.
Muhammad is the Arabic name Muslims use for God.
No — Muslims worship Allah alone; Muhammad is honoured as the final prophet and messenger, but he is human and is never worshipped.
The Buddha is the Hindu god of wisdom.
Muhammad is the Arabic name Muslims use for God.
Muslims worship Muhammad in the way Christians worship Jesus.
